content: Patients who are lost to follow-up (LTFU), have stopped treatment (STOP), or have changed regimens will be categorized as such until a more recent event occurs. For instance, if a patient is classified as LTFU at month 4, they will be recorded as LTFU in the month 6 column. However, if the patient returns by month 8, they will then be recorded as RESTART (with the corresponding regimen code) and will be counted in rows H, I, or J, instead of being classified as LTFU. In cases of regimen changes, only the most recent change should be recorded. For example, when reporting 12-month outcomes for a cohort, if a patient switches from regimen 1a to 2a at month 7 and then switches from 2a to 3a at month 8, this should be recorded as a switch to a third-line regimen. It should not be recorded as a switch to a second-line regimen, as this would result in the patient being counted twice. Baseline data for cohorts starting antiretroviral therapy (ART) in July 2019 should include their outcomes at 6 months (January 2020), 12 months (July 2020), and 24 months (July 2021). Similarly, for cohorts starting ART in August 2019, baseline data should include outcomes at 6 months (February 2020), 12 months (August 2020), and 24 months (August 2021). For cohorts starting ART by month and year, data should be reported at baseline, then at 6 months, 12 months, and 24 months of ART. For example, the cohort starting ART in July 2019 should have data reported for 6 months (January 2020), 12 months (July 2020), and 24 months (July 2021). Similarly, the cohort starting ART in August 2019 should have data reported for 6 months (February 2020), 12 months (August 2020), and 24 months (August 2021).
